title: Bounded-time oracle call implementation
statement: Let $D$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, $O$ a language of Boolean words, and $\tau:\bbn\to\bbn$ a time bound. If $D$ decides $O$ within time $\tau$, then there exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $C$, states $en,ex$ of $C$, and $a\in\bbn$ such that $C$ has at least one work tape, $en\ne ex$, and, for every Boolean word $z$, starting with $z$ on tape $0$ and all other tapes blank, $C$ reaches state $ex$ for the first time at some positive step $t\le a(\tau(|z|)+|z|+2)$; at that step all tapes are blank except that tape $0$ contains the one-symbol word recording whether $z\in O$.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$O$ is a language of Boolean words
